parts.text: When can he see the flame through the holes?

options.text: When the three holes lie on one straight line at the same height.
When the hole in B is moved well above the other two holes.
When light from the flame bends freely around the sheets so hole alignment does not matter.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem:
The diagram shows Vivaan looking at a candle flame through holes in three cardboard sheets A, B and C.

Answer both parts.

part_answers.answer: Light travels in a straight line, so the flame is seen only when the holes are straight and aligned.

teacher.key_rationale: A straight aligned path lets light reach the eye; raising the middle hole or treating light as freely bending around the sheets removes that condition.
teacher.figure_note: Candle and three cardboard sheets with holes on a straight path.
